_comment: Carry destination for issue #1330 (R5-D7-02, the round-5 D7 audit's
cadence-gap finding; judge verdict bug). The stage that needs this is any
later seat that judges or re-measures the sysid two-state fit across a
coordinator cadence gap -- a later round's D7 dimension. No roster group
in this tree claims #1330 (no wave-*-groups.json names D7, the round-5
audit or the issue), so this file is that stage's brief. Shape and
stage: any later seat that judges or re-measures the sysid two-state fit across a coordinator cadence gap (a later round's D7 dimension; tools/audit/briefs/D7.md is its method, tools/audit/round5/D7/seat-a/sysid_step_bias.py its round-5 harness)

carries.from: the pull request that refuses the cadence-gap path of identify_slab by name instead of falling back to the one-state SystemIdentification.identify() (R5-D7-02, #1330; its arm-gate half, #1329, is already merged)
carries.control: The measurement, with the perturbation that would have falsified it. At the merge base 129f96b3 the round-5 D7 harness (tools/audit/round5/D7/seat-a/sysid_step_bias.py, its cadence-gap settle arm) drove a DECLARED plant whose #991 arm gate passes -- a preset with the slab heat transfer multiplied by 100 -- and injected one missed coordinator update (a 2.5 h interval against the 0.25 h cadence). On heavy_old the cell completed at +7.29 % UA bias and the production adoption predicate ADMITTED it at confidence 0.436; on light_new the same shape completed at a much larger bias. The perturbation that separates the substitution from the gap: the one-state regression is already +7.22 % biased on that plant with NO gap at all, and the gap itself supplies 0.07 pp of it -- so the error is the fallback, not the gap, and a fix that clamped the gap would have moved nothing. The null control is the other end: with no gap the same harness reads slab_fit_bias_* at +0.00 % with slab_fit_admitted_* = 1 on every preset, so the refusal this branch adds is the gap's and not the plant's.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this paragraph's numbers: they are the round-5 harness's and this branch's, and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. Run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round5/D7/seat-a/sysid_step_bias.py` from the repository root and read its `RESULT gap_settle_bias_*` and `RESULT gap_settle_admitted_*` lines: the gap arm must be refused on every preset, and the no-gap arm must still complete and still be admitted. Then perturb: shorten the injected interval below the cadence-gap predicate's bound and confirm the two-state fit returns. A later fix that changes which plants the arm gate admits changes which cells of that arm can fire, so re-derive the gate's verdict at your merge base before reading a refusal as this one.
carries.brief: A coordinator cadence gap no longer yields a fit. identify_slab() refuses BY NAME when its interval series carries a gap -- `dts > 2.0` h, the missed-update case -- instead of falling back to the one-state SystemIdentification.identify(), because the arm was granted on a DECLARED two-state plant and the one-state regression fits the model class the experiment exists to replace. Two consequences for a later seat. First, do not build a harness, a golden or a verdict on the assumption that a gapped settle run produces an adopted result: the production path returns `completed=False` with a reason naming the cadence gap, and the adoption gate therefore never sees it. Second, the refusal is NOT the slow-slab refusal. The #991 predicate check still runs FIRST, so a plant refused for its slab mode keeps the `slab mode too slow` reason and the #942 protection is untouched; the new reason appears only on plants that passed that predicate. When you price the effect of a gap, separate the substitution's bias from the gap's contribution -- the fallback's one-state regression is biased on these plants with no gap at all, so attributing the whole observed bias to the gap overstates it by an order of magnitude. Re-establish both figures at your own merge base by running the no-gap arm beside the gapped one.
